title: Keep failure detection separate from consensus recovery
description: Select a server topology, inject an infrastructure event, and choose the read contract. The model shows which operations still have evidence-backed availability.

topologies.label: One datacenter, 3 servers
topologies.detail: The smallest recommended production voting set. It tolerates one failed server.

topologies.label: One datacenter, 5 servers
topologies.detail: A larger voting set that tolerates two failures, with more consensus work per write.

topologies.label: Two datacenters, 3 + 3 servers
topologies.detail: Two independent Raft clusters joined for cross-datacenter Consul features.
topologies.boundary: A quorum is evaluated inside each datacenter

readModes.label: Default read
readModes.detail: Use the leader lease path used by most HTTP API reads.
readModes.availabilityNote: Fast and authoritative enough for most reads, but unavailable when the datacenter cannot maintain leadership.

readModes.label: Consistent read
readModes.detail: Require the leader to confirm authority with a quorum.
readModes.availabilityNote: Strongest read contract, with extra latency and no response without quorum.

readModes.label: Stale read
readModes.detail: Allow any reachable server to answer from its local replicated state.
readModes.availabilityNote: Can remain available without a leader, but freshness has no fixed upper bound unless the caller enforces one.

incidents.label: Lose one primary voter
incidents.detail: One server is unavailable; the remaining peers can still communicate.
incidents.actionWithQuorum: Confirm the remaining leader and voters, replace the failed server through the normal peer lifecycle, and verify snapshots before another failure.
incidents.actionWithoutQuorum: Do not add random peers. Establish the actual surviving peer set and follow the documented outage-recovery procedure.
incidents.unsafeAction: Restart every server at once or enable bootstrap mode on multiple servers.
evidence: consul operator raft list-peers shows one leader and the expected voters
consul.autopilot.healthy and leader telemetry remain stable
Catalog writes and a synthetic registration still commit

incidents.label: Lose two primary voters
incidents.detail: Two servers are unavailable. A five-server cluster still has quorum; a three-server cluster does not.
incidents.actionWithQuorum: Replace one failed voter at a time and wait for the peer set and Autopilot health to stabilize before continuing.
incidents.actionWithoutQuorum: Freeze topology changes, collect peer evidence, and use the documented manual recovery or a tested snapshot restore.
incidents.unsafeAction: Treat gossip membership as proof that Raft can still commit writes.
evidence: The number of alive voters still meets the calculated quorum
A current leader is visible in raft list-peers
The applied index advances when a controlled write is issued

incidents.label: Partition the datacenters
incidents.detail: Each datacenter can reach its local peers, but WAN federation traffic is interrupted.
incidents.actionWithQuorum: Keep local discovery local, pause cross-datacenter changes, verify primary/secondary replication state, and restore the federation path before relying on remote services.
incidents.actionWithoutQuorum: Recover the affected datacenter's local quorum first; WAN membership cannot substitute for local Raft consensus.
incidents.unsafeAction: Assume federation automatically moves application traffic or merges conflicting writes.
evidence: Local raft list-peers remains healthy in each datacenter
WAN members and gateway telemetry identify the broken federation path
Remote discovery and ACL or intention replication lag are measured explicitly

incidents.label: Overload the leader path
incidents.detail: The voters are alive, but disk sync, CPU, or request pressure delays Raft and leader-served reads.
incidents.actionWithQuorum: Reduce abusive reads and writes, move eligible discovery traffic to stale or agent-cached paths, and scale server resources using telemetry evidence.
incidents.actionWithoutQuorum: Remove overload before forcing recovery; a slow cluster can look failed while destructive topology changes make recovery harder.
incidents.unsafeAction: Set max_stale aggressively so overloaded followers forward even more reads to the leader.
evidence: raft leader last-contact, election, and commit latency remain within the runbook threshold
RPC rate-limit errors and server saturation are correlated with callers
Synthetic DNS, default-read, and write probes are measured separately
